items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: And you’d listen to them and then say oh my God, they’re mutilating the melody, the chord changes are so basic, and after you’re listening — you know you’re listening to Oscar Peterson and Bud Powell and Wynton Kelly — you’re listening to all these guys and Shearing, oh.

ctx.x: Walk the bar and all that stuff.

Yeah. So it was a little detrimental and I just ignored them, I didn’t even listen. Like all those tunes from the Doo Wop tunes, they’re good tunes too. I can enjoy them now. But then they were just pushing us out of work. So I just, as far as I was concerned, and then some of them they didn’t do the right chords or melody line. There was one group that sang [sings] I told every little star/just how sweet I think you are/why haven’t I told you. Then on the bridge they completely screwed it up. They changed the…

simplistic you know. And then when they started the Beatles, now the Beatles, when you study their music they are something else. They’ve got standards out. They’ve got tunes that you can play for anybody. “Michelle.” [sings] Yesterday [scats] beautiful you know? “Norwegian Wood.” Oh man. But then there’s a lot of these other groups, but what they had, the mile high amplifiers and the roar of sound that practically knocks you over, and they’re prancing on the stage, even breaking up instruments on the stage you…
